1	// Program Buffer execution helpers for the RISC-V Debug Module.
2	//
3	// Follows the same duck-typed template pattern as dmi_poll.hpp so that
4	// resume_driver.hpp can include this header without a circular dependency.
5	// Bus type requirement: write(uint8_t reg, uint32_t val) and
6	//                       read(uint8_t reg) -> uint32_t.
7	//
8	// Debug Spec references: section 3.6 (Program Buffer), table 3.1 (DMI),
9	// section 3.7.1.3 (Abstract Command - Access Register).
10	
11	#pragma once
12	
13	#include "hybrid/abstract_command.hpp"
14	#include "hybrid/dmi_poll.hpp"
15	
16	#include <array>
17	#include <cstdint>
18	#include <span>
19	#include <stdexcept>
20	#include <string>
21	
22	namespace hybrid {
23	
24	// DMI address of the first Program Buffer register (progbuf0..progbuf15).
25	inline constexpr uint8_t kProgbuf0 = 0x20u;
26	
27	// Max payload instructions: 16 total slots minus 1 reserved for the
28	// mandatory ebreak that terminates execution.
29	inline constexpr std::size_t kProgbufMaxInsns = 15u;
30	
31	// Standard ebreak encoding (funct12=1, opcode=SYSTEM).
32	inline constexpr uint32_t kEbreak = 0x00100073u;
33	
34	// "Execute Program Buffer only" command (Debug Spec table 3.1):
35	//   cmdtype  = 0 (Access Register)
36	//   aarsize  = Bits64 (3) - ignored by DM when transfer=0, set for consistency
37	//   postexec = 1 (bit 18)
38	//   transfer = 0 (bit 17 NOT set) - skip register I/O, only run progbuf
39	//   write    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
40	//   regno    = 0 (irrelevant when transfer=0)
41	inline constexpr uint32_t kExecProgbufCmd =
42	    (uint32_t(AarSize::Bits64) & 0x7u) << 20 | (1u << 18);
43	
44	// Encode `vsetvl rd, rs1, rs2` (RVV 1.0 section 6.2, funct7=1000000).
45	// Tier-B restore: stage vl in rs1 and vtype in rs2 via Abstract Commands,
46	// then branch-free-restore both in one Program Buffer execution.
47	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vsetvl(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, uint8_t rs2)
48	{
49	    return (0b1000000u << 25)
50	         | ((uint32_t(rs2) & 0x1Fu) << 20)
51	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
52	         | (0b111u << 12)
53	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
54	         | 0x57u;  // OP-V opcode
55	}
56	
57	// Encode `csrrw rd, csr, rs1` (SYSTEM opcode, funct3=001).
58	// Tier-A PB fallback: stage the CSR value in rs1 via Abstract Command,
59	// then write it to a CSR that the DM cannot reach via abstract access.
60	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_csrrw(uint8_t rd, uint16_t csr, uint8_t rs1)
61	{
62	    return ((uint32_t(csr) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
63	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
64	         | (0b001u << 12)
65	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
66	         | 0x73u;  // SYSTEM opcode
67	}
68	
69	// Encode `vle8.v vd, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector load, EEW=8 (RVV 1.0 sec 7.4).
70	// Fields: vm=1 (unmasked, bit 25), width=000, mop=00, mew=0, nf=000,
71	// lumop=00000, opcode LOAD-FP=0x07. PB V-regfile reload sweeps v0..v31 from
72	// the shared scratch region after a vsetvl to e8/m1.
73	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vle8_v(uint8_t vd, uint8_t rs1)
74	{
75	    return (1u << 25)
76	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
77	         | ((uint32_t(vd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
78	         | 0x07u;  // LOAD-FP opcode
79	}
80	
81	// Encode `vse8.v vs3, (rs1)` - unit-stride vector store, EEW=8. Mirror of
82	// encode_vle8_v with opcode STORE-FP=0x27. PB V-regfile dump sweeps v0..v31
83	// back to the shared scratch region at drain.
84	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_vse8_v(uint8_t vs3, uint8_t rs1)
85	{
86	    return (1u << 25)
87	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
88	         | ((uint32_t(vs3) & 0x1Fu) << 7)
89	         | 0x27u;  // STORE-FP opcode
90	}
91	
92	// Encode `addi rd, rs1, imm12` (OP-IMM opcode 0x13, funct3=000). The batched
93	// V-data sweep advances the scratch base pointer x7 by one register-span
94	// between transfers WITHIN a Program-Buffer execution, so the per-register
95	// abstract x7 write disappears. imm12 is a signed 12-bit field (-2048..2047).
96	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_addi(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
97	{
98	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
99	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
100	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
101	         | 0x13u;  // OP-IMM opcode (funct3=000)
102	}
103	
104	// Encode `ld rd, imm12(rs1)` (LOAD opcode 0x03, funct3=011 for 64-bit). The GPR
105	// block-load sweeps x1..x31 from a scratch region addressed by a base register,
106	// so 31 abstract register writes collapse into a few Program-Buffer executions.
107	inline constexpr uint32_t encode_ld(uint8_t rd, uint8_t rs1, int32_t imm12)
108	{
109	    return ((uint32_t(imm12) & 0xFFFu) << 20)
110	         | ((uint32_t(rs1) & 0x1Fu) << 15)
111	         | (0b011u << 12)
112	         | ((uint32_t(rd)  & 0x1Fu) << 7)
113	         | 0x03u;  // LOAD opcode
114	}
115	
116	// Write insns[0..n-1] to progbuf0..n-1 and kEbreak to progbuf[n].
117	// Clears any sticky abstractcs.cmderr (W1C), issues kExecProgbufCmd, polls
118	// until abstractcs.busy clears, then verifies cmderr stayed clear.
119	//
120	// Throws std::runtime_error if insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns, if the poll
121	// times out, or if the DM raises cmderr during execution. No caller has a
122	// legitimate reason to silently continue on PB failure - the hart state
123	// would be partially restored / partially drained, which is worse than
124	// surfacing the fault.
125	template<typename Bus>
126	inline void exec_progbuf(Bus& bus, std::span<const uint32_t> insns)
127	{
128	    if (insns.size() > kProgbufMaxInsns)
129	        throw std::runtime_error(
130	            "exec_progbuf: too many instructions ("
131	            + std::to_string(insns.size()) + " > "
132	            + std::to_string(kProgbufMaxInsns) + ")");
133	
134	    for (std::size_t i = 0; i < insns.size(); ++i)
135	        bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + i), insns[i]);
136	    bus.write(static_cast<uint8_t>(kProgbuf0 + insns.size()), kEbreak);
137	
138	    if ((bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask) != 0u)
139	        bus.write(kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsCmderrMask);
140	
141	    bus.write(kDmiCommand, kExecProgbufCmd);
142	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy, "exec_progbuf busy");
143	
144	    const uint32_t cmderr = bus.read(kDmiAbstractcs) & kAbstractcsCmderrMask;
145	    if (cmderr != 0u)
146	        throw std::runtime_error(
147	            "exec_progbuf: PB execution raised cmderr="
148	            + std::to_string(cmderr >> 8));
149	}
150	
151	// vtype encoding for e8, m8, ta, ma (vsew=000, vlmul=011, vta=1, vma=1). The
152	// V-data sweep uses LMUL=8 so one vle8.v/vse8.v moves a whole group of 8
153	// registers (8*vlenb byte-elements, vl=8*vlenb) in a single instruction.
154	inline constexpr uint32_t kVtypeE8M8 = 0xC3u;
155	
156	// Abstract-command write of a 64-bit value to Debug Module register `regno`
157	// (GPR/CSR/FPR): DATA0/DATA1 + Access-Register(write) + busy-poll. Free
158	// function so ResumeDriver, StateDrain, and the V-data sweep share one copy.
159	template<typename Bus>
160	inline void write_register_abstract(Bus& bus, uint16_t regno, uint64_t value)
161	{
162	    bus.write(kDmiData0, static_cast<uint32_t>(value & 0xffffffffu));
163	    bus.write(kDmiData1, static_cast<uint32_t>((value >> 32) & 0xffffffffu));
164	    bus.write(kDmiCommand,
165	              access_register_command(regno, AarSize::Bits64, /*write=*/true));
166	    poll_until_clear(bus, kDmiAbstractcs, kAbstractcsBusy,
167	                     "write_register_abstract");
168	}
169	
170	// Sweep all 32 V data registers between the hart regfile and the vlenb-packed
171	// scratch region via the Program Buffer. load=true issues vle8.v
172	// (scratch -> regfile, on resume); load=false issues vse8.v (regfile ->
173	// scratch, at drain). The leading vsetvl to e8/m8 sets vl=8*vlenb and forces
174	// vstart=0, so one unit-stride access covers a whole LMUL=8 group of 8
175	// registers. Uses x5/x6 (vsetvl operands) and x7 (group base pointer) as
176	// scratch. `vlenb` is the runtime per-register width; the scratch must be
177	// packed at vlenb stride (stage_v_to_scratch) so each 8-register group is
178	// contiguous.
179	template<typename Bus>
180	inline void pb_v_data_sweep(Bus& bus, uint64_t scratch_gpa, uint64_t vlenb,
181	                            bool load)
182	{
183	    // The scratch holds v0..v31 packed contiguously at vlenb stride (see
184	    // stage_v_to_scratch), so 8 consecutive registers form one LMUL=8 group.
185	    // One vle8.v/vse8.v then moves a whole group (8*vlenb contiguous bytes,
186	    // vl=8*vlenb) and all 32 registers transfer in 4 grouped ops -- whose 4
187	    // (transfer; addi) pairs fit in a SINGLE Program-Buffer execution. Each PB
188	    // execution is one halted-hart DM round-trip (~1000 sim cycles in the
189	    // busy-poll), so this is the floor: one vsetvl + one grouped execution. The
190	    // register bytes never cross DMI; they ride the shared mmap.
191	    constexpr unsigned     kRegsPerGroup   = 8;  // LMUL=8
192	    // kVtypeE8M8's vlmul field (bits 2:0) must encode this LMUL, so one grouped
193	    // vle8.v/vse8.v really covers kRegsPerGroup registers (integer LMUL=1<<vlmul;
194	    // 0xC3 & 7 == 3 -> LMUL 8).
195	    static_assert((1u << (kVtypeE8M8 & 0x7u)) == kRegsPerGroup,
196	                  "kVtypeE8M8 must encode LMUL = kRegsPerGroup");
197	    constexpr std::size_t  kGroupSweepInsns = (32 / kRegsPerGroup) * 2;  // (ld;addi)*4
198	    static_assert(kGroupSweepInsns <= kProgbufMaxInsns,
199	                  "the grouped sweep must fit one Program Buffer execution");
200	    const uint64_t group_bytes = static_cast<uint64_t>(kRegsPerGroup) * vlenb;
201	    if (group_bytes > 2047)  // addi imm12 is signed 12-bit; max 8*128 = 1024
202	        throw std::runtime_error(
203	            "pb_v_data_sweep: 8*vlenb exceeds the addi imm12 range");
204	
205	    // vsetvl to e8/m8 with AVL = 8*vlenb sets vl = VLMAX = 8*vlenb (one
206	    // byte-element per lane across the whole group) and forces vstart = 0.
207	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(5), group_bytes);  // AVL
208	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(6), kVtypeE8M8);   // e8, m8, ta, ma
209	    const std::array<uint32_t, 1> pb_vsetvl = { encode_vsetvl(0, 5, 6) };
210	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{pb_vsetvl});
211	
212	    // Base pointer x7 staged once; the in-buffer addi advances it one group at
213	    // a time. The group base register must be LMUL-aligned: v0/v8/v16/v24.
214	    write_register_abstract(bus, regno_gpr(7), scratch_gpa);
215	    const uint32_t addi_step =
216	        encode_addi(7, 7, static_cast<int32_t>(group_bytes));
217	    std::array<uint32_t, kGroupSweepInsns> group_sweep{};
218	    std::size_t n = 0;
219	    for (uint8_t g = 0; g < 32; g += kRegsPerGroup) {
220	        group_sweep[n++] = load ? encode_vle8_v(g, 7) : encode_vse8_v(g, 7);
221	        group_sweep[n++] = addi_step;  // last group's addi is harmless dead work
222	    }
223	    exec_progbuf(bus, std::span<const uint32_t>{group_sweep.data(), n});
224	}
225	
226	}  // namespace hybrid

1	// V-register transport staging: the host<->guest-RAM half of the V data
2	// regfile transfer. The Debug Module abstract-command space has no slots for
3	// v0..v31 (the RISC-V Debug Spec leaves V to the Program Buffer or
4	// implementation-specific extensions), so vsim moves v0..v31 by executing a
5	// vle8.v/vse8.v sweep on the halted hart through the Program Buffer (see
6	// pb_v_data_sweep in program_buffer.hpp, driven by ResumeDriver on resume and
7	// StateDrain at drain). That sweep loads/stores the V scratch region of guest
8	// RAM -- the top page of the mapped span (v_scratch_gpa, L26); this header
9	// provides the matching host-side copy:
10	//
11	//   - stage_v_to_scratch: state.vreg[] -> scratch RAM, called before resume so
12	//     the ResumeDriver vle8.v sweep reads QEMU 1's V values.
13	//   - read_v_from_scratch: scratch RAM -> state.vreg[], called after the
14	//     StateDrain vse8.v sweep so the drained v0..v31 land in state.vreg[]
15	//     (the handoff file).
16	//
17	// The transfer is transparent to the workload: benchmark binaries issue no
18	// transport code, only the enter_vsim / exit_vsim markers. rt_c_v_regs.c is
19	// the reference fixture.
20	//
21	// Pure logic: no SystemC, no DMI bus. Easy to unit-test.
22	
23	#pragma once
24	
25	#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
26	
27	#include <cstddef>
28	#include <cstdint>
29	#include <cstring>
30	#include <span>
31	#include <stdexcept>
32	
33	namespace hybrid
34	{
35	
36	// Total scratch bytes needed: 32 V regs × HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX. Sized to the
37	// maximum supported VLEN; the actual per-reg byte count is `vlenb`. Defined in
38	// the shared ABI (HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES) so the driver's mmap sizing and this
39	// consumer agree on one count (L26/F2).
40	inline constexpr std::size_t kVScratchBytes = HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES;
41	
42	// L26: the scratch region is the TOP kVScratchBytes of the mapped RAM span,
43	// not a fixed address. Scheme D parks it just above the program's declared
44	// RAM (the driver maps one page more than --mem-size), so no program layout
45	// can collide with it. This is the single source of truth for the GUEST
46	// address the Program-Buffer sweep (ResumeDriver/StateDrain) loads/stores
47	// through; the host stager below copies span-relative and needs no base.
48	inline constexpr auto v_scratch_gpa(uint64_t ram_base, std::size_t ram_size)
49	  -> uint64_t
50	{
51	  return ram_base + static_cast<uint64_t>(ram_size) - kVScratchBytes;
52	}
53	
54	// Sentinel for "no V scratch configured". ResumeDriver/StateDrain default to
55	// it; a non-V handoff never consults the scratch GPA, so that is fine, but if
56	// a V handoff reaches the sweep with the GPA still unset the driver throws
57	// (loud) rather than silently transporting V through a bogus address.
58	inline constexpr uint64_t kVScratchGpaUnset =
59	  static_cast<uint64_t>(-1);
60	
61	// GPR block-load prototype: x1..x31 (8 bytes each) staged in the TOP of the
62	// scratch page so the resume ld-sweep reads them below the V region (which
63	// grows up from the base). Reusing the V page keeps this single-repo; it only
64	// applies when the V data leaves room (gpr_scratch_fits), else the caller falls
65	// back to per-register abstract writes. A production version would give the GPR
66	// block its own scratch page instead of sharing the V one.
67	inline constexpr std::size_t kGprScratchBytes = 31 * 8;  // x1..x31
68	
69	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_gpa(uint64_t v_scratch_base) -> uint64_t
70	{
71	  return v_scratch_base + kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
72	}
73	
74	inline constexpr auto gpr_scratch_fits(uint64_t vlenb) -> bool
75	{
76	  return static_cast<std::size_t>(32) * vlenb <= kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes;
77	}

79	namespace detail
80	{
81	
82	// Byte offset of the scratch region inside a RAM span: its top page. Throws
83	// if the span is smaller than one scratch page (a too-small RAM mapping).
84	inline auto scratch_offset(std::size_t ram_size) -> std::size_t
85	{
86	  if (ram_size < kVScratchBytes)
87	    throw std::runtime_error(
88	      "v_regfile_xfer: RAM span smaller than the V scratch page");
89	  return ram_size - kVScratchBytes;
90	}
91	
92	}  // namespace detail
93	
94	// Copy state.vreg[] into the span's top scratch page. Called just before vsim
95	// resumes the hart so the fixture can vle8.v from scratch and pick up QEMU 1's
96	// V values.
97	inline void stage_v_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
98	                               std::span<uint8_t> ram)
99	{
100	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
101	  // Pack at vlenb stride (drop the wire-format padding) so v0..v31 sit
102	  // contiguously and the Program-Buffer sweep can move 8 at a time via LMUL=8.
103	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
104	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
105	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + r * vlenb,
106	                state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX, vlenb);
107	}
108	
109	// Copy state.gpr[1..31] into the GPR sub-region (top of the scratch page). x31
110	// lands in the final slot (the mapping's last word); the memory decoder reads
111	// it back fine, so x31 rides the resume ld-sweep like every other GPR -- it is
112	// simply loaded last, being the sweep's own base register. Called before resume
113	// so the ResumeDriver ld-sweep repopulates x1..x31.
114	inline void stage_gpr_to_scratch(const hybrid_state_v1& state,
115	                                 std::span<uint8_t> ram)
116	{
117	  const auto off =
118	    detail::scratch_offset(ram.size()) + (kVScratchBytes - kGprScratchBytes);
119	  for (std::size_t i = 1; i < 32; ++i)
120	    std::memcpy(ram.data() + off + (i - 1) * 8, &state.gpr[i], 8);
121	}
122	
123	// Copy the span's top scratch page into state.vreg[]. Called inside the vsim
124	// drain path after the fixture's prologue vse8.v has settled the (possibly
125	// mutated) regfile bytes into RAM.
126	inline void read_v_from_scratch(hybrid_state_v1& state,
127	                                std::span<const uint8_t> ram)
128	{
129	  const auto off = detail::scratch_offset(ram.size());
130	  // Unpack the vlenb-packed scratch back into the wire-strided vreg[] slots.
131	  // Each slot's padding (bytes vlenb..HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) is left as-is:
132	  // callers pass a passthrough state whose padding is already zero (the QEMU
133	  // drain zero-fills it), so the full 128-byte slots stay byte-identical to the
134	  // oracle that --verify compares against.
135	  const std::size_t vlenb = state.vlenb;
136	  for (std::size_t r = 0; r < 32; ++r)
137	    std::memcpy(state.vreg + r * HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX,
138	                ram.data() + off + r * vlenb, vlenb);
139	}

141	}  // namespace hybrid

9	/**
10	 * A memory region in the range of `[base_address, end_address)`.
11	 * The constructor takes an inclusive end address and stores it as exclusive.
12	 * e.g. memory_region(0x80000000, 0x8fffffff) stores base=0x80000000,
13	 *      end=0x90000000.
14	 */
15	struct MemoryRegion
16	{
17	  using addr_type = uint64_t;
18	
19	  const addr_type base_address; // inclusive
20	  const addr_type end_address; // exclusive (stored as param + 1)
21	
22	  /**
23	   * @param base_address The base address of the memory region (inclusive).
24	   * @param end_address The end address of the memory region (inclusive).
25	   * @throws std::invalid_argument if base_address > end_address.
26	   * @example memory_region(0x00, 0xff) represents [0x00, 0x100)
27	   */
28	  MemoryRegion(const addr_type base_address, const addr_type end_address)
29	      : base_address{base_address}, end_address{end_address + 1}
30	  {
31	    if (base_address > end_address)
32	      throw std::invalid_argument(std::format(
33	        "invalid memory region: [{:#x}-{:#x}]", base_address, end_address));
34	  }
35	
36	  auto contains(const addr_type addr) const noexcept -> bool
37	  {
38	    return addr >= this->base_address && addr < this->end_address;
39	  }
40	
41	  auto contains(const MemoryRegion& other) const noexcept -> bool
42	  {
43	    return other.base_address >= this->base_address
44	        && other.end_address <= this->end_address;
45	  }
46	
47	  // Does this region fully contain the half-open access [addr, addr + len)?
48	  // Takes a raw access (exclusive length) rather than a MemoryRegion, so it
49	  // does NOT go through the inclusive-end ctor (which adds 1). An access whose
50	  // exclusive end lands exactly on end_address is contained, so the final byte
51	  // of the region is reachable. `addr < end_address` keeps end_address - addr
52	  // from underflowing, and comparing len against it avoids overflowing addr +
53	  // len at the top of the address space.
54	  auto contains_access(const addr_type addr,
55	                       const addr_type len) const noexcept -> bool
56	  {
57	    return addr >= this->base_address
58	        && addr < this->end_address
59	        && len <= this->end_address - addr;
60	  }
61	
62	  auto overlaps(const MemoryRegion& other) const noexcept -> bool
63	  {
64	    return this->end_address > other.base_address
65	        && this->base_address < other.end_address;
66	  }
67	};

Confirmed all four claims against the actual code. Here is the review.

## REUSE review - only the code the diff ADDS

**One actionable finding:**

`src/platform/memory_region.hpp:57` | `contains_access`'s first two clauses (`addr >= base_address && addr < end_address`) are byte-for-byte the body of the existing single-address `contains(addr)` at line 38. | Call `this->contains(addr)`, i.e. `return this->contains(addr) && len <= this->end_address - addr;` | Cost: a duplicated bounds expression that must be kept in sync by hand; low severity. Note the *method itself* is justified - the existing range overload `contains(const MemoryRegion&)` can't be reused here because `MemoryRegion{addr, addr+len}` goes through the inclusive-end ctor that adds 1 (that is the off-by-one this diff fixes), so a new raw half-open check is warranted.

**Three claims checked, no duplication - reuse is appropriate:**

- `encode_ld` (`program_buffer.hpp:107`) - not a duplicate. Grep confirms no pre-existing `encode_ld` or generic I-type encoder anywhere in `src/`; the existing encoders are `encode_vsetvl/csrrw/vle8_v/vse8_v/addi`. It sits directly beside `encode_addi` in the same `inline constexpr uint32_t` free-function style. Correct placement, nothing to reuse.

- `restore_gprs_via_pb` batching loop (`resume_driver.hpp:337-355`) - no existing helper does progbufsize-1 chunking, so the hand-rolled loop is not re-implementing anything. `pb_v_data_sweep` (program_buffer.hpp:179) fits all its insns in a *single* `exec_progbuf` (8 <= 15) and never chunks; `exec_progbuf` (program_buffer.hpp:126) caps at the compile-time `kProgbufMaxInsns` and *throws* on overflow rather than splitting. The loop already delegates each batch to `exec_progbuf`, which is the right primitive. Minor consistency nit only (not real duplication): it re-derives the "reserve one slot for ebreak" rule as `progbufsize - 1` and is the sole site reading the runtime `abstractcs.progbufsize`, whereas `exec_progbuf` encodes the same reservation as the compile-time `kProgbufMaxInsns` (16 - 1). Not worth a change.

- `stage_gpr_to_scratch` (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp:114-121`) - already reuses the genuine shared primitive `detail::scratch_offset(ram.size())`, same as `stage_v_to_scratch`. The remaining loop differs in source array (`state.gpr` vs `state.vreg`), stride (fixed 8 vs runtime `vlenb`), index range (1..31 vs 0..31), and sub-region base offset. Factoring a common packer over 2-3 call sites would over-abstract; the shared piece is correctly reused. No finding.

No test files flagged (no whole-helper duplication in them).
